newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INL reshaping Sky proposal - NZ Herald.
newsitem.headline: INL reshaping Sky proposal - NZ Herald.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Ltd, in the throes of buying a 51 percent holding in Sky Network Television, is believed to be contemplating cutting its prospective holding to 40 percent, the New Zealand Herald reported on Thursday.
This would still leave it with effective control while also providing a basis for a float of the pay television operator.
As well, by taking its holding below 50 percent, INL would not land Sky's debt on its balance sheet through having to consolidate the asset.

INL, after one false start, said early this month that it was negotiating to buy the 51 percent Sky stake held by HKP Partners, a United States consortium owned by Bell Atlantic, Ameritech, TCI Communications and Time Warner.
The stake is estimated to be worth about NZ$300 million.
INL managing director Mike Robson was hoping to have the deal sewn up by the end of the month. He also did not rule out a float taking place after the deal with HKP was concluded.
For a successful float other shareholders would need to participate. But it is unlikely that a large percentage of the shares will be put on to the market, at least initially.

Other Sky shareholders, Heatley Jarvis Investments (15.8 percent), Todd Corporation (8.8 percent) and Tappenden Holdings (7.7 percent), are thought to be keen to bring liquidity to their respective holdings.

However, according to broking sources, Heatley Jarvis Investments and Tappenden would not be willing to sell many shares, if any, into a float, preferring the after-market where prices are normally higher.
The other main shareholder, TVNZ, with a 16.2 percent stake, has also said it was a buyer rather than a seller.

But after the Government knocked back New Zealand Post's bid to expand its empire, the chances of TVNZ being given the green light to buy more Sky shares are slim even if it does have a holding in Clear Communications to sell.
